#!/usr/bin/env bash
# --mem-size contract: one model-neutral flag, per-model semantics, plus the
# hybrid V-scratch boundary.
#
#   fast:   forwards --mem-size verbatim to QEMU's `-m`; QEMU itself validates
#           its DRAM ceiling (this AE350 build tops out at 16 GiB). A non-whole-
#           MiB size is rejected by the driver first.
#   hybrid: sizes the shared mmap (= QEMU backend = vsim window). The driver
#           reserves ONE V-scratch page ABOVE program RAM, so the usable window
#           is the 2 GiB AE350 DRAM window MINUS that page. Exactly 2G therefore
#           overflows and is rejected; 2047M is the largest whole-MiB size that
#           fits. See driver/shm.cpp max_program_mem_bytes().
#   cycle:  validate-only (the engine always models its full DRAM window).
#   --mmap-size stays a hidden alias of --mem-size.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"        # engine-portable (fast/cycle)
MELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"        # carries ROI markers (hybrid)
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF (make -C tests/fixtures)"
[ -f "$MELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $MELF (make -C tests/fixtures)"

# hybrid <SIZE> <want-rc> then per-line assertions; runs the command ONCE.
hy() { "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" --log-level 1 "$@" "$MELF" </dev/null 2>&1; }

# --- fast: pass-through to QEMU -m -------------------------------------------
# 1G accepted, program still runs.
expect 0 'hello from vplat' "$BIN" run --mode fast --mem-size 1G "$ELF"
# QEMU's own ceiling: this AE350 build refuses more than 16 GiB (FAILURE case).
expect 1 'Cannot model more than 16GB RAM' "$BIN" run --mode fast --mem-size 32G "$ELF"
# A size that is not a whole MiB: driver rejects before spawning (FAILURE case).
expect 2 'whole MiB' "$BIN" run --mode fast --mem-size 1000 "$ELF"

# --- hybrid: sized shared mmap, capped at the 2 GiB window minus V-scratch ---
# BOUNDARY (FAILURE): exactly 2G overflows by the one reserved V-scratch page;
# the cap fires BEFORE any mmap file is allocated.
out=$(hy --mem-size 2G); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "hybrid --mem-size 2G rc=$rc (want 2):"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "AE350 DRAM window" || fail "hybrid 2G: missing cap message:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap" \
  && fail "hybrid 2G must fail BEFORE allocating the mmap:"$'\n'"$out"

# BOUNDARY (ACCEPT): 2047M is the largest whole-MiB size that fits; the shared
# mmap rounds to 2.0 GiB and the run completes with a cycle figure.
out=$(hy --mem-size 2047M); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid --mem-size 2047M rc=$rc:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap 2.0 GiB" \
  || fail "hybrid 2047M: mmap status should show 2.0 GiB:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "window_cycles" || fail "hybrid 2047M: no cycle figure:"$'\n'"$out"

# mid-size: mmap sized to the request, run completes.
out=$(hy --mem-size 256M); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid --mem-size 256M rc=$rc:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap 256.0 MiB" \
  || fail "hybrid 256M: mmap status should show 256.0 MiB:"$'\n'"$out"

# the retired --mmap-size spelling still works (hidden alias).
out=$(hy --mmap-size 192M); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--mmap-size alias rc=$rc:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap 192.0 MiB" \
  || fail "alias: mmap status should show 192.0 MiB:"$'\n'"$out"

# --- cycle: validated, declared a no-op, run still passes --------------------
expect 0 'nothing to size' \
  "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 64M "$ELF"

ok "--mem-size contract (fast forwards to QEMU ceiling; hybrid capped at 2G-Vscratch: 2G rejected, 2047M max; cycle no-op; alias)"

lines: || fail "hybrid 2047M: mmap status should show 2.0 GiB:"$'\n'"$out"

"""Build docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb for the andesim repo."""
import nbformat as nbf

nb = nbf.v4.new_notebook()
nb.metadata["kernelspec"] = {
    "display_name": "Python 3",
    "language": "python",
    "name": "python3",
}

md = nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell
code = nbf.v4.new_code_cell

cells = []

cells.append(md("""\
# andesim quickstart: hybrid mode with the marker trigger

This notebook runs real `./andesim` commands and shows their real output.
It covers the simplest measuring flow:

1. Check the install.
2. Run a prebuilt ELF in hybrid mode with `--trigger marker`.
3. Write, compile, and measure your own C program with ROI markers.
4. Preview a run with `--dry-run`.

**What hybrid mode does:** QEMU (fast, functional) runs your program until
the ROI start marker. Then it hands the full CPU state and memory to the
cycle-accurate engine (vsim, built from real RTL), which runs only your
region-of-interest (ROI) and reports how many cycles it took.

**Prerequisites:** a built andesim install (see `README.md`). Run this
notebook from the repo (it lives in `docs/`; the first cell moves to the
repo root). You can serve it with `scripts/notebook_server.sh`.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
# Move to the repo root (the notebook lives in docs/).
import os
if not os.path.exists("./andesim"):
    %cd ..
assert os.path.exists("./andesim"), "run this notebook from the andesim repo"
print("repo root:", os.getcwd())\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 1: check the install

`./andesim doctor` is a read-only health report. A healthy install ends
with `0 FAIL`. It also lists the engines and where the shared memory for
hybrid runs will live (`mmap tiers`).
"""))

cells.append(code("!./andesim doctor"))

cells.append(md("""\
`./andesim list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts. Hybrid mode needs
one `vsim:` (cycle-accurate) engine. With more than one installed, you
must pick one with `--engine`.
"""))

cells.append(code("!./andesim list engines"))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 2: first hybrid run with a prebuilt ELF

The install ships ready-made test ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`.
`rt_c_hello.elf` already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger marker`
works out of the box.

The command has three required parts:

- `--mode hybrid` picks the model.
- `--trigger marker` says the ROI is the span between the markers in the
  binary.
- `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` picks the cycle-accurate engine.

(`run` is the default command, so you may also drop the word `run`:
`./andesim --mode hybrid ...` works the same.)
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
How to read the output:

- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
- `[marker window_cycles] N` is the answer: the ROI took N cycles on this
  engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window.
- The run ends after the ROI. Code after the end marker never executes:
  hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.

Note: the FIRST hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds
slower. andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
`~/.cache/andesim/`, so later runs skip restoring registers that still
hold reset values. This never changes results.

By default (`--log-level 2`, info) andesim prints only your program's
output and the cycle figure. `--log-level 1` (debug, same scale as the
vsim engines: 0=trace .. 6=off) adds the driver's chatter -- the resolved
engine banner and the shared-memory (`[andesim] mmap`) line:
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --log-level 1 tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 3: measure your own program

Wrap the region you want to measure with the two ROI markers from
`<andesim/ROI.h>` (shipped with the runtime):

```c
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

andesim_ROI_begin();
my_kernel(a, b, c);
andesim_ROI_end();
```

The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so the
same binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real
silicon.

Measurement hygiene: keep the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))`
function called between the markers, and pass inputs/outputs through
memory. This stops the compiler from moving your compute out of the
measured window.

The cell below writes a small dot-product program to a temp directory.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
import pathlib, tempfile

WORK = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="andesim_nb_"))
(WORK / "dot_product.c").write_text(r'''
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

#define N 64

static int a[N], b[N];
static volatile long result;

__attribute__((noinline))
long dot_product(const int *x, const int *y, int n) {
    long sum = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        sum += (long)x[i] * y[i];
    return sum;
}

int main(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = N - i; }

    printf("setup done, entering ROI\\n");

    andesim_ROI_begin();
    result = dot_product(a, b, N);
    andesim_ROI_end();

    /* never reached in a hybrid run -- the run ends at the ROI exit */
    printf("dot product = %ld\\n", result);
    return 0;
}
''')
print("wrote", WORK / "dot_product.c")\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
Compile with your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `doctor` reports), linked
against the andesim runtime:

- `-B build/runtime` points gcc at the runtime artifacts (use an absolute
  path when compiling outside the repo).
- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's startup code and linker
  script, so one ELF runs on every engine (no semihosting).
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
import re, subprocess

# Take the toolchain path from doctor so the notebook is not tied to one host.
doctor = subprocess.run(["./andesim", "doctor"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
GCC = re.search(r"riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc\\s+(\\S+)", doctor).group(1)
print("toolchain:", GCC)

!{GCC} -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \\
    -B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs \\
    {WORK}/dot_product.c -o {WORK}/dot_product.elf && echo COMPILED\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
Now measure it. Same command as step 2, only the ELF changed:
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium {WORK}/dot_product.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
`[marker window_cycles]` is the cycle cost of `dot_product(a, b, 64)` on
the ax45mpv_premium core: the call, the multiply-accumulate loop, and the
store to `result` -- and nothing else. Boot, `printf`, and the loop that
filled the arrays all ran on the fast QEMU leg and cost zero measured
cycles.

Note `dot product = ...` is missing from the output: it sits after
`andesim_ROI_end()`, and a hybrid run stops at the ROI exit.
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 4: preview a run with `--dry-run`

`--dry-run` prints the exact engine command lines (both legs for hybrid)
and runs nothing. Use it to see precisely what a run will execute.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --dry-run {WORK}/dot_product.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Where to go next

- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` -- every option, one by one. Section 5.3 covers
  the second trigger (`--trigger pc`) for binaries you cannot edit.
- `--verify` (guide section 5.7) cross-checks a hybrid run against a
  pure-QEMU oracle, field by field.
- `--kanata` (guide section 5.8) writes a pipeline trace of exactly the
  measured window.
"""))

nb.cells = cells
path = "docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb"
nbf.write(nb, path)
print("wrote", path)

"""Build docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb for the andesim repo."""
import nbformat as nbf

nb = nbf.v4.new_notebook()
nb.metadata["kernelspec"] = {
    "display_name": "Python 3",
    "language": "python",
    "name": "python3",
}

md = nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell
code = nbf.v4.new_code_cell

cells = []

cells.append(md("""\
# andesim quickstart: hybrid mode with the marker trigger

This notebook runs real `./andesim` commands and shows their real output.
It covers the simplest measuring flow:

1. Check the install.
2. Run a prebuilt ELF in hybrid mode with `--trigger marker`.
3. Write, compile, and measure your own C program with ROI markers.
4. Preview a run with `--dry-run`.

**What hybrid mode does:** QEMU (fast, functional) runs your program until
the ROI start marker. Then it hands the full CPU state and memory to the
cycle-accurate engine (vsim, built from real RTL), which runs only your
region-of-interest (ROI) and reports how many cycles it took.

**Prerequisites:** a built andesim install (see `README.md`). Run this
notebook from the repo (it lives in `docs/`; the first cell moves to the
repo root). You can serve it with `scripts/notebook_server.sh`.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
# Move to the repo root (the notebook lives in docs/).
import os
if not os.path.exists("./andesim"):
    %cd ..
assert os.path.exists("./andesim"), "run this notebook from the andesim repo"
print("repo root:", os.getcwd())\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 1: check the install

`./andesim doctor` is a read-only health report. A healthy install ends
with `0 FAIL`. It also lists the engines and where the shared memory for
hybrid runs will live (`mmap tiers`).
"""))

cells.append(code("!./andesim doctor"))

cells.append(md("""\
`./andesim list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts. Hybrid mode needs
one `vsim:` (cycle-accurate) engine. With more than one installed, you
must pick one with `--engine`.
"""))

cells.append(code("!./andesim list engines"))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 2: first hybrid run with a prebuilt ELF

The install ships ready-made test ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`.
`rt_c_hello.elf` already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger marker`
works out of the box.

The command has three required parts:

- `--mode hybrid` picks the model.
- `--trigger marker` says the ROI is the span between the markers in the
  binary.
- `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` picks the cycle-accurate engine.

(`run` is the default command, so you may also drop the word `run`:
`./andesim --mode hybrid ...` works the same.)
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
How to read the output:

- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
- `[andesim] N cycles` is the answer: the ROI took N cycles on this
  engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window.
- The run ends after the ROI. Code after the end marker never executes:
  hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.

Note: the FIRST hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds
slower. andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
`~/.cache/andesim/`, so later runs skip restoring registers that still
hold reset values. This never changes results.

By default (`--log-level 2`, info) andesim prints only your program's
output and the cycle figure. `--log-level 1` (debug, same scale as the
vsim engines: 0=trace .. 6=off) adds the driver's chatter -- the resolved
engine banner and the shared-memory (`[andesim] mmap`) line:
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --log-level 1 tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 3: measure your own program

Wrap the region you want to measure with the two ROI markers from
`<andesim/ROI.h>` (shipped with the runtime):

```c
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

andesim_ROI_begin();
my_kernel(a, b, c);
andesim_ROI_end();
```

The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so the
same binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real
silicon.

Measurement hygiene: keep the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))`
function called between the markers, and pass inputs/outputs through
memory. This stops the compiler from moving your compute out of the
measured window.

The cell below writes a small dot-product program to a temp directory.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
import pathlib, tempfile

WORK = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="andesim_nb_"))
(WORK / "dot_product.c").write_text(r'''
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

#define N 64

static int a[N], b[N];
static volatile long result;

__attribute__((noinline))
long dot_product(const int *x, const int *y, int n) {
    long sum = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        sum += (long)x[i] * y[i];
    return sum;
}

int main(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = N - i; }

    printf("setup done, entering ROI\\n");

    andesim_ROI_begin();
    result = dot_product(a, b, N);
    andesim_ROI_end();

    /* never reached in a hybrid run -- the run ends at the ROI exit */
    printf("dot product = %ld\\n", result);
    return 0;
}
''')
print("wrote", WORK / "dot_product.c")\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
Compile with your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `doctor` reports), linked
against the andesim runtime:

- `-B build/runtime` points gcc at the runtime artifacts (use an absolute
  path when compiling outside the repo).
- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's startup code and linker
  script, so one ELF runs on every engine (no semihosting).
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
import re, subprocess

# Take the toolchain path from doctor so the notebook is not tied to one host.
doctor = subprocess.run(["./andesim", "doctor"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
GCC = re.search(r"riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc\\s+(\\S+)", doctor).group(1)
print("toolchain:", GCC)

!{GCC} -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \\
    -B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs \\
    {WORK}/dot_product.c -o {WORK}/dot_product.elf && echo COMPILED\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
Now measure it. Same command as step 2, only the ELF changed:
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium {WORK}/dot_product.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
`[andesim] N cycles` is the cycle cost of `dot_product(a, b, 64)` on
the ax45mpv_premium core: the call, the multiply-accumulate loop, and the
store to `result` -- and nothing else. Boot, `printf`, and the loop that
filled the arrays all ran on the fast QEMU leg and cost zero measured
cycles.

Note `dot product = ...` is missing from the output: it sits after
`andesim_ROI_end()`, and a hybrid run stops at the ROI exit.
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 4: preview a run with `--dry-run`

`--dry-run` prints the exact engine command lines (both legs for hybrid)
and runs nothing. Use it to see precisely what a run will execute.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --dry-run {WORK}/dot_product.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Where to go next

- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` -- every option, one by one. Section 5.3 covers
  the second trigger (`--trigger pc`) for binaries you cannot edit.
- `--verify` (guide section 5.7) cross-checks a hybrid run against a
  pure-QEMU oracle, field by field.
- `--kanata` (guide section 5.8) writes a pipeline trace of exactly the
  measured window.
"""))

nb.cells = cells
path = "docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb"
nbf.write(nb, path)
print("wrote", path)

# Debug-Logging Roadmap: log levels -> reproducible bugs

Goal: use the `--log-level` scale (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error
5=critical 6=off, shared with vsim) so that any failed or suspicious run
can be REPRODUCED and diagnosed from its own output, without re-running
under ad-hoc printf debugging.

Principles
- info (default) stays clean: program output + the answer line. All new
  detail goes to debug/trace.
- errors always print, and every error should carry enough to reproduce.
- one scale end-to-end: andesim driver -> QEMU plugin -> vsim engine.
- input/output of every feature is a printable contract a test can grep.

Current state (done)
- driver/log.hpp/.cpp: threshold + log_on(level); --log-level flag.
- info: `[andesim] N cycles`; debug: banner, mmap line, window mcycle
  detail, PASS; warn: unsupported-CSR + mem-size notes.

---

## L0. log_line helper (structural)

- Description: route the existing leveled fprintf sites through one
  `log_line(level, fmt, ...)` helper (uniform `[andesim]` prefix, one
  place to add a file sink later). No behavior change.
- Key files: driver/log.hpp, driver/log.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp,
  driver/shm.cpp
- Depends on: nothing
- State: TODO

## L1. trace prints the exact leg commands + exit status

- Description: at trace (0), before spawning each leg print the fully
  resolved command line (reuse the --dry-run renderer), and after it the
  exit code + wall time. Contract:
    `[andesim] exec fast-leg [qemu64]: qemu-system-riscv64 -object ...`
    `[andesim] exec accurate-leg [vsim:x]: sim_x my.elf --resume-from-qemu ...`
    `[andesim] exit fast-leg: rc=0 wall=2.1s`
  Debugging one leg becomes copy-paste of one line.
- Key files: driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/argv.hpp
- Depends on: L0
- State: TODO

## L2. repro block on failure (error level, always on)

- Description: when a leg fails, times out, or --verify mismatches, KEEP
  the run's small artifacts -- handoff state file, .ilm/.dlm/.hvm
  sidecars, staged qemu -readconfig cfg (not the big mmap by default) --
  under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/<utc-timestamp>-<elf-stem>/`, then print
  an error-level block: kept paths, engine id + --describe build hash,
  ELF sha256, and the exact command(s) to re-run each leg against the
  kept files. A bug report becomes "attach this directory".
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/process.cpp
- Depends on: L1 (same command renderer)
- State: TODO

## L3. debug decision log

- Description: at debug, print every resolution the driver makes, so a
  "wrong figure" report shows WHERE the run diverged from expectation:
  engine choice (and why: sole engine / --engine), ISA+VLEN sync values,
  pc-trigger resolution (`symbol -> 0x...`), mem-size parse, mmap tier
  (exists), reset-baseline cache hit/miss + cache path, write-mask
  summary (`restored 12 governed CSRs, skipped 39`; per-CSR names at
  trace).
- Key files: driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/hybrid.cpp,
  driver/engine_registry.cpp
- Depends on: L0
- State: TODO

## L4. one flag drives the whole pipeline

- Description: forward the level to both legs. vsim leg: append
  `--log-level N` verbatim (same scale by design) and, at <= debug,
  relay its stderr (prefixed `[vsim]`) instead of dropping it at
  capture. QEMU plugin: new `log_level=N` plugin arg; at debug it prints
  drain decisions to stderr (trigger hit pc, flags word, vlenb, sidecar
  sizes written, state file path).
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/vsim_filter.cpp,
  qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c
- Depends on: L0
- State: TODO

## L5. --log-file: full trace to a file, console unchanged

- Description: `--log-file <path>` writes ALL leveled messages
  (trace..error) with timestamps to the file regardless of the console
  threshold; the failure repro block (L2) names the file. One run, one
  complete capsule to attach to a bug.
- Key files: driver/log.hpp, driver/log.cpp, driver/cli.cpp,
  driver/main.cpp
- Depends on: L0 (every message must flow through log_line), L2
- State: TODO

---

## V-side (external hybrid_vsim repo; separate sessions there)

vsim already has spdlog + --log-level; these map the hybrid orchestration
onto it. Can be delegated to a subagent working in the vsim checkout
(pair with the csr-transport-bringup skill).

- V1. debug: resume/drain phase summaries -- counts per block (GPR/FPR/
  CSR/V), liveness-gate skip count, per-phase simulated-cycle cost.
- V2. trace: per-op log -- each abstract command / progbuf batch with
  CSR addr, value, cmderr result (the exec_progbuf fault-hunting pain).
- V3. resume-abort diagnostics: on abort print the failing step, CSR,
  drained-vs-WARL value, and an engine-caps hint.
- Key files (vsim repo): src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp,
  src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp, src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp
- Depends on: nothing on the andesim side; L4 makes them reachable from
  one andesim flag.

---

Rollout: one feature per session, TDD-first (each feature's contract is
grep-able, so its RED test goes in tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_log_*.sh
or the vsim repo's ctest). Update docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 5.10 as each
lands, and re-execute docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb when the
default-visible surface changes.

Compound effect: L2+L5 make every failure self-documenting; L4 makes one
flag capture the whole pipeline; V2 turns state-transport faults from
printf-archaeology into a diff of two trace files. Over time, bug
reports converge to "attach the repro dir + log file".

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Log-level contract: driver chatter is leveled like vsim's --log-level
# (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off; default 2=info).
#
#   1. default (info): a hybrid --dry-run shows the dry-run commands but NO
#      banner and NO mmap line.
#   2. --log-level 1 (debug): banner + mmap line appear; the mmap line uses
#      the [andesim] prefix and the retired [hsim mmap] prefix is gone.
#   3. default (info) on a real hybrid run: program output + the cycle
#      figure only -- no banner, no mmap line, no trailing PASS chatter.
#   4. an out-of-range --log-level is a clean non-zero error naming 0..6.
#
# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not wired
# into run_e2e.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
ENGINE="vsim:ax45mpv_premium"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF"

# 1. default level hides the banner and the mmap line (dry-run: cheap)
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "dry-run: 2 command(s)" || fail "dry-run header missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "default level should hide the banner:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "default level should hide the mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"

# 2. debug level shows them, with the [andesim] prefix (no [hsim mmap])
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --log-level 1 --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" || fail "debug level missing banner:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap" || fail "debug level missing [andesim] mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[hsim mmap\]" && fail "[hsim mmap] prefix must be gone:"$'\n'"$out"

# 3. default level on a real hybrid run: program output + cycle figure only;
#    the answer line uses the same [andesim] N cycles shape as cycle mode,
#    with the raw mcycle detail reserved for debug.
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "hello from QEMU1" || fail "program output missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' || fail "cycle figure missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "window_cycles" && fail "old window_cycles format leaked:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "mcycle=" && fail "mcycle detail leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "banner leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "mmap line leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "^PASS:" && fail "PASS chatter leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"

echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] window: trigger=marker vsim mcycle=[0-9]+ qemu mcycle=[0-9]+$' \

"$BIN" --mode fast --log-level 9 "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1 && fail "--log-level 9 should exit non-zero"

# Debug-Logging Roadmap: log levels -> reproducible bugs

Goal: use the `--log-level` scale (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error
5=critical 6=off, shared with vsim) so that any failed or suspicious run
can be REPRODUCED and diagnosed from its own output, without re-running
under ad-hoc printf debugging.

Principles
- info (default) stays clean: program output + the answer line. All new
  detail goes to debug/trace.
- errors always print, and every error should carry enough to reproduce.
- one scale end-to-end: andesim driver -> QEMU plugin -> vsim engine.
- input/output of every feature is a printable contract a test can grep.

Current state (done)
- driver/log.hpp/.cpp: threshold + log_on(level); --log-level flag.
- info: `[andesim] N cycles`; debug: banner, mmap line, window mcycle
  detail, PASS; warn: unsupported-CSR + mem-size notes.

---

## L0. log_line helper (structural)

- Description: route the existing leveled fprintf sites through one
  `log_line(level, fmt, ...)` helper (uniform `[andesim]` prefix, one
  place to add a file sink later). No behavior change.
- Key files: driver/log.hpp, driver/log.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp,
  driver/shm.cpp
- Depends on: nothing
- State: TODO

## L1. trace prints the exact leg commands + exit status

- Description: at trace (0), before spawning each leg print the fully
  resolved command line (reuse the --dry-run renderer), and after it the
  exit code + wall time. Contract:
    `[andesim] exec fast-leg [qemu64]: qemu-system-riscv64 -object ...`
    `[andesim] exec accurate-leg [vsim:x]: sim_x my.elf --resume-from-qemu ...`
    `[andesim] exit fast-leg: rc=0 wall=2.1s`
  Debugging one leg becomes copy-paste of one line.
- Key files: driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/argv.hpp
- Depends on: L0
- State: TODO

## L2. repro block on failure (error level, always on)

- Description: when a leg fails, times out, or --verify mismatches, KEEP
  the run's small artifacts -- handoff state file, .ilm/.dlm/.hvm
  sidecars, staged qemu -readconfig cfg (not the big mmap by default) --
  under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/<utc-timestamp>-<elf-stem>/`, then print
  an error-level block: kept paths, engine id + --describe build hash,
  ELF sha256, and the exact command(s) to re-run each leg against the
  kept files. A bug report becomes "attach this directory".
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/process.cpp
- Depends on: L1 (same command renderer)
- State: TODO

## L3. debug decision log

- Description: at debug, print every resolution the driver makes, so a
  "wrong figure" report shows WHERE the run diverged from expectation:
  engine choice (and why: sole engine / --engine), ISA+VLEN sync values,
  pc-trigger resolution (`symbol -> 0x...`), mem-size parse, mmap tier
  (exists), reset-baseline cache hit/miss + cache path, write-mask
  summary (`restored 12 governed CSRs, skipped 39`; per-CSR names at
  trace).
- Key files: driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/hybrid.cpp,
  driver/engine_registry.cpp
- Depends on: L0
- State: TODO

## L4. one flag drives the whole pipeline

- Description: forward the level to both legs. vsim leg: append
  `--log-level N` verbatim (same scale by design) and, at <= debug,
  relay its stderr (prefixed `[vsim]`) instead of dropping it at
  capture. QEMU plugin: new `log_level=N` plugin arg; at debug it prints
  drain decisions to stderr (trigger hit pc, flags word, vlenb, sidecar
  sizes written, state file path).
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/vsim_filter.cpp,
  qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c
- Depends on: L0
- State: TODO

## L5. --log-file: full trace to a file, console unchanged

- Description: `--log-file <path>` writes ALL leveled messages
  (trace..error) with timestamps to the file regardless of the console
  threshold; the failure repro block (L2) names the file. One run, one
  complete capsule to attach to a bug.
- Key files: driver/log.hpp, driver/log.cpp, driver/cli.cpp,
  driver/main.cpp
- Depends on: L0 (every message must flow through log_line), L2
- State: TODO

## V-side (external hybrid_vsim repo; separate sessions there)

vsim already has spdlog + --log-level; these map the hybrid orchestration
onto it. Can be delegated to a subagent working in the vsim checkout
(pair with the csr-transport-bringup skill).

- V1. debug: resume/drain phase summaries -- counts per block (GPR/FPR/
  CSR/V), liveness-gate skip count, per-phase simulated-cycle cost.
- V2. trace: per-op log -- each abstract command / progbuf batch with
  CSR addr, value, cmderr result (the exec_progbuf fault-hunting pain).
- V3. resume-abort diagnostics: on abort print the failing step, CSR,
  drained-vs-WARL value, and an engine-caps hint.
- Key files (vsim repo): src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp,
  src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp, src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp
- Depends on: nothing on the andesim side; L4 makes them reachable from
  one andesim flag.

grep-able, so its RED test goes in tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_log_*.sh
or the vsim repo's ctest). Update docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 5.10 as each

can be REPRODUCED and diagnosed from its own output, without re-running
under ad-hoc printf debugging.

Principles
- info (default) stays clean: program output + the answer line. All new
  detail goes to debug/trace.
- errors always print, and every error should carry enough to reproduce.
- one scale end-to-end: andesim driver -> QEMU plugin -> vsim engine.
- input/output of every feature is a printable contract a test can grep.

Current state (done)
- driver/log.hpp/.cpp: threshold + log_on(level); --log-level flag.
- info: `[andesim] N cycles`; debug: banner, mmap line, window mcycle
  detail, PASS; warn: unsupported-CSR + mem-size notes.

---

## L0. log_line helper (structural)

- Description: route the existing leveled fprintf sites through one
  `log_line(level, fmt, ...)` helper (uniform `[andesim]` prefix, one
  place to add a file sink later). No behavior change.
- Key files: driver/log.hpp, driver/log.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp,
  driver/shm.cpp
- Depends on: nothing
- State: TODO

## L1. trace prints the exact leg commands

- Description: at trace (0), before spawning each leg print the fully
  resolved command line (same renderer as --dry-run). Contract:
    `[andesim] exec fast-leg [qemu64]: qemu-system-riscv64 -object ...`
    `[andesim] exec accurate-leg [vsim:x]: sim_x my.elf --resume-from-qemu ...`
  Debugging one leg becomes copy-paste of one line.
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/argv.hpp
- Depends on: nothing (landed before L0; migrate to log_line with L0)
- State: DONE (test: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_log_level.sh 3b/3c)

## L2. repro block on failure (error level, always on)

- Description: when a leg fails, times out, or --verify mismatches, KEEP
  the run's small artifacts -- handoff state file, .ilm/.dlm/.hvm
  sidecars, staged qemu -readconfig cfg (not the big mmap by default) --
  under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/<utc-timestamp>-<elf-stem>/`, then print
  an error-level block: kept paths, engine id + --describe build hash,
  ELF sha256, and the exact command(s) to re-run each leg against the
  kept files. A bug report becomes "attach this directory".
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/process.cpp
- Depends on: L1 (same command renderer)
- State: TODO

## L3. debug decision log

- Description: at debug, print every resolution the driver makes, so a
  "wrong figure" report shows WHERE the run diverged from expectation:
  engine choice (and why: sole engine / --engine), ISA+VLEN sync values,
  pc-trigger resolution (`symbol -> 0x...`), mem-size parse, mmap tier
  (exists), reset-baseline cache hit/miss + cache path, write-mask
  summary (`restored 12 governed CSRs, skipped 39`; per-CSR names at
  trace).
- Key files: driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/hybrid.cpp,
  driver/engine_registry.cpp
- Depends on: L0
- State: TODO

## L4. one flag drives the whole pipeline

- Description: forward the level to both legs. vsim leg: append
  `--log-level N` verbatim (same scale by design) and, at <= debug,
  relay its stderr (prefixed `[vsim]`) instead of dropping it at
  capture. QEMU plugin: new `log_level=N` plugin arg; at debug it prints
  drain decisions to stderr (trigger hit pc, flags word, vlenb, sidecar
  sizes written, state file path).
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/vsim_filter.cpp,
  qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c
- Depends on: L0
- State: TODO

## L5. --log-file: full trace to a file, console unchanged

- Description: `--log-file <path>` writes ALL leveled messages
  (trace..error) with timestamps to the file regardless of the console
  threshold; the failure repro block (L2) names the file. One run, one
  complete capsule to attach to a bug.
- Key files: driver/log.hpp, driver/log.cpp, driver/cli.cpp,
  driver/main.cpp
- Depends on: L0 (every message must flow through log_line), L2
- State: TODO

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Repro-bundle contract (L2): a failed hybrid leg keeps the evidence.
#
#   1. A hybrid run whose marker trigger never fires FAILS and prints an
#      error-level `[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at <dir>` line.
#      The dir contains manifest.txt (error + per-leg commands) and a copy
#      of the ELF.
#   2. Bundles are pruned to the newest 20 (old ones are removed).
#   3. A successful run keeps nothing and prints no repro line.
#
# Uses XDG_CACHE_HOME to sandbox the bundle root.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
GOODELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"     # has ROI markers
BADELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"     # no markers -> trigger never fires
ENGINE="vsim:ax45mpv_premium"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

CACHE=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$CACHE"' EXIT
REPRO="$CACHE/andesim/repro"

# 1. failing run keeps a bundle and says where
out=$(XDG_CACHE_HOME="$CACHE" timeout 120 "$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
        --engine "$ENGINE" "$BADELF" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "markerless hybrid run should fail:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] repro: kept run artifacts at " \
  || fail "missing repro line:"$'\n'"$out"
dir=$(echo "$out" | sed -n 's/.*kept run artifacts at \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)
[ -d "$dir" ] || fail "repro dir does not exist: $dir"
[ -f "$dir/manifest.txt" ] || fail "manifest.txt missing in $dir"
grep -q "fast-leg" "$dir/manifest.txt" || fail "manifest missing fast-leg command"
grep -q "error:" "$dir/manifest.txt" || fail "manifest missing error"
[ -f "$dir/vplat_hello.elf" ] || fail "ELF copy missing in $dir"

# 2. prune to the newest 20
for i in $(seq -w 1 25); do mkdir -p "$REPRO/000000${i}-old"; done
XDG_CACHE_HOME="$CACHE" timeout 120 "$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
  --engine "$ENGINE" "$BADELF" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
n=$(ls -1 "$REPRO" | wc -l)
[ "$n" -le 20 ] || fail "repro bundles not pruned: $n dirs remain"

# 3. success keeps nothing new
before=$(ls -1 "$REPRO" | wc -l)
out=$(XDG_CACHE_HOME="$CACHE" timeout 180 "$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
        --engine "$ENGINE" "$GOODELF" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "good run failed:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "repro:" && fail "success printed a repro line:"$'\n'"$out"
after=$(ls -1 "$REPRO" | wc -l)
[ "$after" -eq "$before" ] || fail "success created a bundle ($before -> $after)"

ok "repro bundle on failure (kept + manifest + ELF, pruned to 20, silent on success)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off; default 2=info).
#
#   1. default (info): a hybrid --dry-run shows the dry-run commands but NO
#      banner and NO mmap line.
#   2. --log-level 1 (debug): banner + mmap line appear; the mmap line uses
#      the [andesim] prefix and the retired [hsim mmap] prefix is gone.
#   3. default (info) on a real hybrid run: program output + the cycle
#      figure only -- no banner, no mmap line, no trailing PASS chatter.
#   4. an out-of-range --log-level is a clean non-zero error naming 0..6.
#
# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not wired
# into run_e2e.sh.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Log-level contract: driver chatter is leveled like vsim's --log-level
# (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off; default 2=info).
#
#   1. default (info): a hybrid --dry-run shows the dry-run commands but NO
#      banner and NO mmap line.
#   2. --log-level 1 (debug): banner + mmap line appear; the mmap line uses
#      the [andesim] prefix and the retired [hsim mmap] prefix is gone.
#   3. default (info) on a real hybrid run: program output + the cycle
#      figure only -- no banner, no mmap line, no trailing PASS chatter.
#   4. an out-of-range --log-level is a clean non-zero error naming 0..6.
#
# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not wired
# into run_e2e.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
ENGINE="vsim:ax45mpv_premium"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF"

# 1. default level hides the banner and the mmap line (dry-run: cheap)
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "dry-run: 2 command(s)" || fail "dry-run header missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "default level should hide the banner:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "default level should hide the mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"

# 2. debug level shows them, with the [andesim] prefix (no [hsim mmap])
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --log-level 1 --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" || fail "debug level missing banner:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap" || fail "debug level missing [andesim] mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[hsim mmap\]" && fail "[hsim mmap] prefix must be gone:"$'\n'"$out"

# Debug-Logging Roadmap: log levels -> reproducible bugs

Goal: use the `--log-level` scale (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error
5=critical 6=off, shared with vsim) so that any failed or suspicious run
can be REPRODUCED and diagnosed from its own output, without re-running
under ad-hoc printf debugging.

Principles
- info (default) stays clean: program output + the answer line. All new
  detail goes to debug/trace.
- errors always print, and every error should carry enough to reproduce.
- one scale end-to-end: andesim driver -> QEMU plugin -> vsim engine.
- input/output of every feature is a printable contract a test can grep.

Current state (done)
- driver/log.hpp/.cpp: threshold + log_on(level); --log-level flag.
- info: `[andesim] N cycles`; debug: banner, mmap line, window mcycle
  detail, PASS; warn: unsupported-CSR + mem-size notes.

---

## L0. log_line helper (structural)

- Description: route the existing leveled fprintf sites through one
  `log_line(level, fmt, ...)` helper (uniform `[andesim]` prefix, one
  place to add a file sink later). No behavior change.
- Key files: driver/log.hpp, driver/log.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp,
  driver/shm.cpp
- Depends on: nothing
- State: TODO

## L1. trace prints the exact leg commands

- Description: at trace (0), before spawning each leg print the fully
  resolved command line (same renderer as --dry-run). Contract:
    `[andesim] exec fast-leg [qemu64]: qemu-system-riscv64 -object ...`
    `[andesim] exec accurate-leg [vsim:x]: sim_x my.elf --resume-from-qemu ...`
  Debugging one leg becomes copy-paste of one line.
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/argv.hpp
- Depends on: nothing (landed before L0; migrate to log_line with L0)
- State: DONE (test: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_log_level.sh 3b/3c)

## L2. repro block on failure (error level, always on)

- Description: when a leg fails, times out, or --verify mismatches, KEEP
  the run's small artifacts -- handoff state file, .ilm/.dlm/.hvm
  sidecars, staged qemu -readconfig cfg (not the big mmap by default) --
  under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/<utc-timestamp>-<elf-stem>/`, then print
  an error-level block: kept paths, engine id + --describe build hash,
  ELF sha256, each leg's exit code + wall time, and the exact command(s)
  to re-run each leg against the kept files. A bug report becomes
  "attach this directory".
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/process.cpp
- Depends on: L1 (same command renderer)
- State: TODO

## L3. debug decision log

- Description: at debug, print every resolution the driver makes, so a
  "wrong figure" report shows WHERE the run diverged from expectation:
  engine choice (and why: sole engine / --engine), ISA+VLEN sync values,
  pc-trigger resolution (`symbol -> 0x...`), mem-size parse, mmap tier
  (exists), reset-baseline cache hit/miss + cache path, write-mask
  summary (`restored 12 governed CSRs, skipped 39`; per-CSR names at
  trace).
- Key files: driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/hybrid.cpp,
  driver/engine_registry.cpp
- Depends on: L0
- State: TODO

## L4. one flag drives the whole pipeline

- Description: forward the level to both legs. vsim leg: append
  `--log-level N` verbatim (same scale by design) and, at <= debug,
  relay its stderr (prefixed `[vsim]`) instead of dropping it at
  capture. QEMU plugin: new `log_level=N` plugin arg; at debug it prints
  drain decisions to stderr (trigger hit pc, flags word, vlenb, sidecar
  sizes written, state file path).
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/vsim_filter.cpp,
  qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c
- Depends on: L0
- State: TODO

## L5. --log-file: full trace to a file, console unchanged

- Description: `--log-file <path>` writes ALL leveled messages
  (trace..error) with timestamps to the file regardless of the console
  threshold; the failure repro block (L2) names the file. One run, one
  complete capsule to attach to a bug.
- Key files: driver/log.hpp, driver/log.cpp, driver/cli.cpp,
  driver/main.cpp
- Depends on: L0 (every message must flow through log_line), L2
- State: TODO

---

## V-side (external hybrid_vsim repo; separate sessions there)

vsim already has spdlog + --log-level; these map the hybrid orchestration
onto it. Can be delegated to a subagent working in the vsim checkout
(pair with the csr-transport-bringup skill).

- V1. debug: resume/drain phase summaries -- counts per block (GPR/FPR/
  CSR/V), liveness-gate skip count, per-phase simulated-cycle cost.
- V2. trace: per-op log -- each abstract command / progbuf batch with
  CSR addr, value, cmderr result (the exec_progbuf fault-hunting pain).
- V3. resume-abort diagnostics: on abort print the failing step, CSR,
  drained-vs-WARL value, and an engine-caps hint.
- Key files (vsim repo): src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp,
  src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp, src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp
- Depends on: nothing on the andesim side; L4 makes them reachable from
  one andesim flag.

---

Rollout: one feature per session, TDD-first (each feature's contract is
grep-able, so its RED test goes in tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_log_*.sh
or the vsim repo's ctest). Update docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 5.10 as each
lands, and re-execute docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb when the
default-visible surface changes.

Compound effect: L2+L5 make every failure self-documenting; L4 makes one
flag capture the whole pipeline; V2 turns state-transport faults from
printf-archaeology into a diff of two trace files. Over time, bug
reports converge to "attach the repro dir + log file".

# Debug-Logging Roadmap: log levels -> reproducible bugs

Goal: use the `--log-level` scale (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error
5=critical 6=off, shared with vsim) so that any failed or suspicious run
can be REPRODUCED and diagnosed from its own output, without re-running
under ad-hoc printf debugging.

Principles
- info (default) stays clean: program output + the answer line. All new
  detail goes to debug/trace.
- errors always print, and every error should carry enough to reproduce.
- one scale end-to-end: andesim driver -> QEMU plugin -> vsim engine.
- input/output of every feature is a printable contract a test can grep.

Current state (done)
- driver/log.hpp/.cpp: threshold + log_on/log_line/log_result; --log-level
  and --log-file flags.
- info: `[andesim] N cycles`; debug: banner, mmap line, window mcycle
  detail, PASS, decision log; trace: exec command lines; warn:
  unsupported-CSR + mem-size notes.
- All of L0..L5 below are DONE (contract test:
  tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_log_level.sh + test_andes_sim_repro.sh).
  Remaining work: the V-side items (external hybrid_vsim repo).

---

## L0. log_line helper (structural)

- Description: route the existing leveled fprintf sites through one
  `log_line(level, fmt, ...)` helper (uniform `[andesim]` prefix, one
  place to add a file sink later). No behavior change.
- Key files: driver/log.hpp, driver/log.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp,
  driver/shm.cpp
- Depends on: nothing
- State: DONE

## L1. trace prints the exact leg commands

- Description: at trace (0), before spawning each leg print the fully
  resolved command line (same renderer as --dry-run). Contract:
    `[andesim] exec fast-leg [qemu64]: qemu-system-riscv64 -object ...`
    `[andesim] exec accurate-leg [vsim:x]: sim_x my.elf --resume-from-qemu ...`
  Debugging one leg becomes copy-paste of one line.
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/argv.hpp
- Depends on: nothing (landed before L0; migrate to log_line with L0)
- State: DONE (test: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_log_level.sh 3b/3c)

## L2. repro block on failure (error level, always on)

- Description: when a leg fails, times out, or --verify mismatches, KEEP
  the run's small artifacts -- handoff state file, .ilm/.dlm/.hvm
  sidecars, staged qemu -readconfig cfg (not the big mmap by default) --
  under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/<utc-timestamp>-<elf-stem>/`, then print
  an error-level block: kept paths, engine id + --describe build hash,
  ELF sha256, each leg's exit code + wall time, and the exact command(s)
  to re-run each leg against the kept files. A bug report becomes
  "attach this directory".
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/process.cpp
- Depends on: L1 (same command renderer)
- State: DONE (test: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_repro.sh)

## L3. debug decision log

- Description: at debug, print every resolution the driver makes, so a
  "wrong figure" report shows WHERE the run diverged from expectation:
  engine choice (and why: sole engine / --engine), ISA+VLEN sync values,
  pc-trigger resolution (`symbol -> 0x...`), mem-size parse, mmap tier
  (exists), reset-baseline cache hit/miss + cache path, write-mask
  summary (`restored 12 governed CSRs, skipped 39`; per-CSR names at
  trace).
- Key files: driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/hybrid.cpp,
  driver/engine_registry.cpp
- Depends on: L0
- State: DONE

## L4. one flag drives the whole pipeline

- Description: forward the level to both legs. vsim leg: append
  `--log-level N` verbatim (same scale by design) and, at <= debug,
  relay its stderr (prefixed `[vsim]`) instead of dropping it at
  capture. QEMU plugin: new `log_level=N` plugin arg; at debug it prints
  drain decisions to stderr (trigger hit pc, flags word, vlenb, sidecar
  sizes written, state file path).
- Key files: driver/run_plan.cpp, driver/vsim_filter.cpp,
  qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c
- Depends on: L0
- State: DONE

## L5. --log-file: full trace to a file, console unchanged

- Description: `--log-file <path>` writes ALL leveled messages
  (trace..error) with timestamps to the file regardless of the console
  threshold; the failure repro block (L2) names the file. One run, one
  complete capsule to attach to a bug.
- Key files: driver/log.hpp, driver/log.cpp, driver/cli.cpp,
  driver/main.cpp
- Depends on: L0 (every message must flow through log_line), L2
- State: DONE

---

## V-side (external hybrid_vsim repo; separate sessions there)

vsim already has spdlog + --log-level; these map the hybrid orchestration
onto it. Can be delegated to a subagent working in the vsim checkout
(pair with the csr-transport-bringup skill).

- V1. debug: resume/drain phase summaries -- counts per block (GPR/FPR/
  CSR/V), liveness-gate skip count, per-phase simulated-cycle cost.
- V2. trace: per-op log -- each abstract command / progbuf batch with
  CSR addr, value, cmderr result (the exec_progbuf fault-hunting pain).
- V3. resume-abort diagnostics: on abort print the failing step, CSR,
  drained-vs-WARL value, and an engine-caps hint.
- Key files (vsim repo): src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp,
  src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp, src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp
- Depends on: nothing on the andesim side; L4 makes them reachable from
  one andesim flag.

---

Rollout: one feature per session, TDD-first (each feature's contract is
grep-able, so its RED test goes in tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_log_*.sh
or the vsim repo's ctest). Update docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 5.10 as each
lands, and re-execute docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb when the
default-visible surface changes.

Compound effect: L2+L5 make every failure self-documenting; L4 makes one
flag capture the whole pipeline; V2 turns state-transport faults from
printf-archaeology into a diff of two trace files. Over time, bug
reports converge to "attach the repro dir + log file".

### 5.10 `--log-level <0-6>` -- how much andesim says

The same scale as the vsim engines' own `--log-level`, so you learn one
scheme: `0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off`.
Default is `2` (info): you see your program's output, the answer line
(`[andesim] N cycles`), and any warnings or errors -- nothing else.
`--log-level 1` adds the driver's chatter: the hybrid banner
(engine/VLEN/trigger), the shared-mmap line (section 5.4), the window
detail (`[andesim] window: trigger=... vsim mcycle=... qemu mcycle=...`,
the two counters behind the delta), and the closing PASS line.
`--log-level 0` additionally prints, just before each hybrid leg runs,
its fully resolved command line (`[andesim] exec fast-leg [qemu64]: ...`)
-- the same text `--dry-run` shows, copy-pasteable to re-run one leg by
hand. Your program's own output is never filtered at any level.

### 5.10 `--log-level <0-6>` (+ `--log-file`) -- how much andesim says

The same scale as the vsim engines' own `--log-level`, so you learn one
scheme: `0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off`.
Default is `2` (info): you see your program's output, the answer line
(`[andesim] N cycles`), and any warnings or errors -- nothing else.

`--log-level 1` (debug) adds the driver's chatter: the hybrid banner
(engine/VLEN/trigger), the decision lines (which engine and why; what
your `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` resolved to), the shared-mmap line (section
5.4), the window detail (`[andesim] window: trigger=... vsim mcycle=...
qemu mcycle=...`), and the closing PASS line. The level also rides into
both hybrid legs: the vsim engine gets the same `--log-level`, the QEMU
handoff plugin gets `log_level=`, and their stderr streams live to your
terminal (at info and above it is silenced), so one flag tunes the whole
pipeline.

`--log-level 0` (trace) additionally prints, just before each hybrid leg
runs, its fully resolved command line (`[andesim] exec fast-leg
[qemu64]: ...`) -- the same text `--dry-run` shows, copy-pasteable to
re-run one leg by hand.

`--log-file <file>` appends EVERY level's messages -- timestamped and
level-tagged, regardless of the console `--log-level` -- to `<file>`.
Run once with `--log-file`, attach the file to a bug report, and nothing
needs re-running. Your program's own output is never filtered at any
level.

Related (always on, any level): when a hybrid leg fails, andesim keeps
the run's evidence -- the drained state files, LM sidecars, the staged
QEMU config, a copy of your ELF, and a `manifest.txt` with the error and
every leg's exact command -- under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` (newest 20
kept) and prints where:

```

```

19	namespace hybrid
20	{
21	
22	template<typename Trigger>
23	class HandoffController
24	{
25	public:
26	  // scratch_gpa (L26): forwarded to StateDrain for the V dump sweep; defaults
27	  // to the unset sentinel (non-V drains never read it). The simulator passes
28	  // the real mmap-top-page GPA. caps: the target core's Andes-CSR support,
29	  // forwarded to StateDrain so the drain re-read skips CSRs the core lacks.
30	  HandoffController(Trigger trigger, DmiBus& bus,
31	                    uint64_t scratch_gpa = kVScratchGpaUnset,
32	                    AndesCaps caps = AndesCaps::all())
33	      : trigger_{std::move(trigger)}, drain_{bus, scratch_gpa, caps}
34	  {}
35	
36	  // Snapshot of the QEMU 1 input state. When set, drain merges FP/CSR/V
37	  // fields from the snapshot into the freshly drained GPRs+PC, avoiding
38	  // a per-field DM Abstract Command on every handoff.
39	  void set_passthrough_input(hybrid_state_v1 input)
40	  {
41	    passthrough_ = input;
42	  }
43	
44	  // #1: when enabled, an EXIT drains only mcycle/minstret (StateDrain::
45	  // drain_counters_only) and passes every other field through from the
46	  // passthrough snapshot, instead of reading back the full register file. The
47	  // driver turns this on whenever --verify is off, where only the vsim mcycle
48	  // delta is consumed -- so the ~190 full-drain abstract commands are wasted.
49	  void set_minimal_drain(bool on)
50	  {
51	    minimal_drain_ = on;
52	  }
53	
54	  // v5: forward the engine's L2C presence + MMIO base to the exit drain, so it
55	  // re-reads the writable L2C config registers for --verify (dual of the resume
56	  // side's set_l2c). Off unless the engine has an L2C.
57	  void set_l2c(bool present, uint64_t base) { drain_.set_l2c(present, base); }
58	
59	  auto on_retire(uint64_t pc) -> std::optional<hybrid_state_v1>
60	  {
61	    const auto hit = trigger_.lookup(pc);
62	    // Only EXIT drains; entry is QEMU's job, vsim ignores ENTER.
63	    if (!hit || hit->kind != HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT)
64	      return std::nullopt;
65	    if (passthrough_)
66	      return minimal_drain_ ? drain_.drain_counters_only(*passthrough_)
67	                            : drain_.drain_with_passthrough(*passthrough_);
68	    return drain_.drain();
69	  }
70

# Debug-Logging Roadmap: log levels -> reproducible bugs

Goal: use the `--log-level` scale (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error
5=critical 6=off, shared with vsim) so that any failed or suspicious run
can be REPRODUCED and diagnosed from its own output, without re-running
under ad-hoc printf debugging.

Principles
- info (default) stays clean: program output + the answer line. All new
  detail goes to debug/trace.
- errors always print, and every error should carry enough to reproduce.
- one scale end-to-end: andesim driver -> QEMU plugin -> vsim engine.
- input/output of every feature is a printable contract a test can grep.

Current state (done)
- driver/log.hpp/.cpp: threshold + log_on/log_line/log_result; --log-level
  and --log-file flags.
- info: `[andesim] N cycles`; debug: banner, mmap line, window mcycle
  detail, PASS, decision log; trace: exec command lines; warn:
  unsupported-CSR + mem-size notes.
- All of L0..L5 below are DONE (contract test:
  tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_log_level.sh + test_andes_sim_repro.sh).
  Remaining work: the V-side items (external hybrid_vsim repo).

---

## L0. log_line helper (structural)

- Description: route the existing leveled fprintf sites through one
  `log_line(level, fmt, ...)` helper (uniform `[andesim]` prefix, one
  place to add a file sink later). No behavior change.
- Key files: driver/log.hpp, driver/log.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp,
  driver/shm.cpp
- Depends on: nothing
- State: DONE

## L1. trace prints the exact leg commands

- Description: at trace (0), before spawning each leg print the fully

1	# andesim User Guide
2	
3	Audience: an engineer who wants to RUN programs on the Andes simulators
4	through `./andesim` and measure cycle counts. This guide covers every
5	user-facing option and feature.
6	
7	It assumes andesim and its engines are already installed and built
8	(QEMU, the vsim engines, the plugin, the runtime, and the test ELFs are
9	prebuilt). If something is missing, run `./andesim doctor` and hand the
10	report to whoever owns your install; building is covered in `README.md`,
11	not here.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. What andesim is
16	
17	andesim runs one RISC-V ELF on one of three models:
18	
19	| Model    | What runs                              | Speed          | You get                    |
20	|----------|----------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
21	| `fast`   | QEMU only (functional)                 | MHz-class      | program output, fast        |
22	| `cycle`  | one cycle-accurate engine, from reset  | kHz-class      | program output + total cycles |
23	| `hybrid` | QEMU fast-forwards, then the cycle engine measures one region you choose | fast until your region | program output + cycles of JUST your region |
24	
25	`hybrid` is the headline feature: QEMU races through boot and setup, then
26	hands the complete architectural state and memory to the cycle-accurate
27	engine (vsim, built from the real RTL), which runs only your
28	region-of-interest (ROI). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta
29	across that window. You mark the window with a **trigger**: source-level
30	markers or a pair of PCs (section 5.3).
31	
32	One run models ONE core. The cycle engine defines the hardware (ISA,
33	VLEN, caches); in hybrid mode the QEMU leg automatically inherits that
34	engine's ISA and VLEN so both legs execute the same architecture.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 2. Check your installation
39	
40	```sh
41	./andesim doctor          # read-only health report
42	./andesim list models     # the three models
43	./andesim list engines    # every engine you can pass to --engine
44	```
45	
46	`doctor` checks artifacts, toolchain, runtime, engines, and the shared-memory
47	backing tiers, and prints WSL2 advice where relevant. A healthy install ends
48	with `Summary: N PASS, 0 FAIL`.
49	
50	`list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts:
51	
52	```
53	ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN
54	qemu64                 qemu  functional      64    -     -     -
55	qemu32                 qemu  functional      32    -     -     -
56	vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
57	vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
58	```
59	
60	`qemu64`/`qemu32` are the functional engines (`fast`); the `vsim:<cfg>`
61	entries are the cycle-accurate engines (`cycle`, and the measuring leg of
62	`hybrid`). `-` means the engine does not report that parameter.
63	
64	Run `./andesim run -h` any time for the compact flag list; this guide is
65	the long version.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## 3. First runs
70	
71	The install ships ready-made ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`; the examples
72	below use them. Replace with your own ELF once you have one (section 4).
73	
74	### 3.1 fast -- functional, full speed
75	
76	```sh
77	./andesim run --mode fast tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
78	```
79	
80	```
81	hello from vplat
82	```
83	
84	Output is the program's own output, verbatim (QEMU passthrough). The exit
85	code of your program becomes the process exit code.
86	
87	### 3.2 cycle -- one engine, from reset, total cycles
88	
89	```sh
90	./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
91	```
92	
93	```
94	hello from vplat
95	[andesim] 4247 cycles
96	```
97	
98	The engine's startup banner and verbose info log are filtered out so the
99	result stands alone; real warnings/errors still pass through, and the
100	program's exit code is propagated. The figure is the whole run from reset
101	-- boot, runtime init, everything.
102	
103	### 3.3 hybrid -- fast-forward, then measure your region
104	
105	`hybrid` needs a trigger that says where the measured window starts and
106	ends. The fixture below already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger
107	marker` works out of the box:
108	
109	```sh
110	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
111	  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
112	```
113	
114	```
115	[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_hello
116	[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.5 GiB)
117	hello from QEMU1
118	[marker window_cycles] 54  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
119	PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_hello)
120	```
121	
122	Reading the output:
123	
124	- The banner names the resolved engine, its VLEN, and the trigger.
125	- `[hsim mmap]` names the shared-memory file backing the run (section 5.4).
126	- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
127	- `[marker window_cycles] 54` is the answer: your ROI took 54 cycles on
128	  this engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window.
129	- The run ends after the ROI. Code after your ROI never executes in a
130	  hybrid run -- hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.
131	
132	The first hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds slower:
133	andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
134	`~/.cache/andesim/` so later runs can skip restoring registers that still
135	hold reset values (typically ~4x faster on the vsim leg). The cache
136	refreshes itself when the engine or the ELF changes.
137	
138	---
139	
140	## 4. Prepare your own program
141	
142	### 4.1 Compile once, run on every engine
143	
144	Link against the andesim runtime and one ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
145	and across a `hybrid` handoff -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting:
146	
147	```sh
148	riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
149	  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
150	```
151	
152	- Use your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `./andesim doctor` reports).
153	- `-B` points gcc at the runtime artifacts; use the absolute path when
154	  compiling outside the repo.
155	- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's `crt0.o`, links
156	  `andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and pins the library order, so no
157	  semihosting library can leak into the link.
158	- Add `v` to `-march` (e.g. `rv64gcv`) for RVV code.
159	
160	For rv32 targets use the rv32 compiler and the rv32 runtime flavor:
161	
162	```sh
163	riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O2 \
164	  -B <andesim>/build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
165	```
166	
167	Custom build system (no gcc driver)? Link the pieces directly:
168	
169	```sh
170	... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
171	  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
172	  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
173	```
174	
175	What the runtime gives your program, on every engine:
176	
177	| Channel          | Behavior                                                       |
178	|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
179	| stdio (fd 0-2)   | `printf` etc. go to the simulator console (a modeled UART)     |
180	| exit code        | `exit(n)` (n < 256) terminates the simulation; `n` becomes the simulator process exit code |
181	| file io (fd > 2) | `open`/`read`/`write` pass through to host files, resolved against the engine's working directory |
182	
183	A `printf` inside a measured ROI works -- but it adds the real UART cycles
184	to your figure. Keep measured kernels I/O-free when you want clean numbers.
185	
186	### 4.2 Mark your region (ROI markers)
187	
188	For `--trigger marker`, wrap the region you want to measure:
189	
190	```c
191	#include <andesim/ROI.h>   /* shipped with the runtime; rides the -B flag */
192	
193	andesim_ROI_begin();
194	my_kernel(a, b, c);
195	andesim_ROI_end();
196	```
197	
198	The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so a marker

1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim <cmd> [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
9	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
10	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
11	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
12	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
13	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
14	
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	struct Cli {
21	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
22	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
23	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
24	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
25	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
26	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
27	  // parsed where they are used.
28	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
29	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
30	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
31	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
32	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
33	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
34	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
35	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
36	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
37	  bool print_memmap = false;              // --print-memmap (run --mode hybrid)
38	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --mode hybrid)
39	  bool gdb = false;                       // --gdb (fast: QEMU gdbstub; cycle: vsim JTAG + ICEman)
40	  std::string gdb_port;                   // --gdb-port (fast: default 1234; cycle: default 9104)

attachment.snippet:
1	# andesim User Guide
2	
3	Audience: an engineer who wants to RUN programs on the Andes simulators
4	through `./andesim` and measure cycle counts. This guide covers every
5	user-facing option and feature.
6	
7	It assumes andesim and its engines are already installed and built
8	(QEMU, the vsim engines, the plugin, the runtime, and the test ELFs are
9	prebuilt). If something is missing, run `./andesim doctor` and hand the
10	report to whoever owns your install; building is covered in `README.md`,
11	not here.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. What andesim is
16	
17	andesim runs one RISC-V ELF on one of three models:
18	
19	| Model    | What runs                              | Speed          | You get                    |
20	|----------|----------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
21	| `fast`   | QEMU only (functional)                 | MHz-class      | program output, fast        |
22	| `cycle`  | one cycle-accurate engine, from reset  | kHz-class      | program output + total cycles |
23	| `hybrid` | QEMU fast-forwards, then the cycle engine measures one region you choose | fast until your region | program output + cycles of JUST your region |
24	
25	`hybrid` is the headline feature: QEMU races through boot and setup, then
26	hands the complete architectural state and memory to the cycle-accurate
27	engine (vsim, built from the real RTL), which runs only your
28	region-of-interest (ROI). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta
29	across that window. You mark the window with a **trigger**: source-level
30	markers or a pair of PCs (section 5.3).
31	
32	One run models ONE core. The cycle engine defines the hardware (ISA,
33	VLEN, caches); in hybrid mode the QEMU leg automatically inherits that
34	engine's ISA and VLEN so both legs execute the same architecture.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 2. Check your installation
39	
40	```sh
41	./andesim doctor          # read-only health report
42	./andesim list models     # the three models
43	./andesim list engines    # every engine you can pass to --engine
44	```
45	
46	`doctor` checks artifacts, toolchain, runtime, engines, and the shared-memory
47	backing tiers, and prints WSL2 advice where relevant. A healthy install ends
48	with `Summary: N PASS, 0 FAIL`.
49	
50	`list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts:
51	
52	```
53	ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN
54	qemu64                 qemu  functional      64    -     -     -
55	qemu32                 qemu  functional      32    -     -     -
56	vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
57	vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
58	```
59	
60	`qemu64`/`qemu32` are the functional engines (`fast`); the `vsim:<cfg>`
61	entries are the cycle-accurate engines (`cycle`, and the measuring leg of
62	`hybrid`). `-` means the engine does not report that parameter.
63	
64	Run `./andesim run -h` any time for the compact flag list; this guide is
65	the long version.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## 3. First runs
70	
71	The install ships ready-made ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`; the examples
72	below use them. Replace with your own ELF once you have one (section 4).
73	
74	### 3.1 fast -- functional, full speed
75	
76	```sh
77	./andesim run --mode fast tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
78	```
79	
80	```
81	hello from vplat
82	```
83	
84	Output is the program's own output, verbatim (QEMU passthrough). The exit
85	code of your program becomes the process exit code.
86	
87	### 3.2 cycle -- one engine, from reset, total cycles
88	
89	```sh
90	./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
91	```
92	
93	```
94	hello from vplat
95	[andesim] 4247 cycles
96	```
97	
98	The engine's startup banner and verbose info log are filtered out so the
99	result stands alone; real warnings/errors still pass through, and the
100	program's exit code is propagated. The figure is the whole run from reset
101	-- boot, runtime init, everything.
102	
103	### 3.3 hybrid -- fast-forward, then measure your region
104	
105	`hybrid` needs a trigger that says where the measured window starts and
106	ends. The fixture below already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger
107	marker` works out of the box:
108	
109	```sh
110	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
111	  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
112	```
113	
114	```
115	hello from QEMU1
116	[andesim] 54 cycles
117	```
118	
119	Reading the output:
120	
121	- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
122	- `[andesim] 54 cycles` is the answer: your ROI took 54 cycles on
123	  this engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window (the same
124	  line shape `cycle` mode prints, but here it covers JUST your ROI).
125	- The run ends after the ROI. Code after your ROI never executes in a
126	  hybrid run -- hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.
127	- Want more detail? `--log-level 1` (section 5.10) adds the driver's
128	  chatter: the resolved engine/VLEN/trigger banner and the shared-memory
129	  line (`[andesim] mmap ...`, section 5.4).
130	
131	The first hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds slower:
132	andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
133	`~/.cache/andesim/` so later runs can skip restoring registers that still
134	hold reset values (typically ~4x faster on the vsim leg). The cache
135	refreshes itself when the engine or the ELF changes.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## 4. Prepare your own program
140	
141	### 4.1 Compile once, run on every engine
142	
143	Link against the andesim runtime and one ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
144	and across a `hybrid` handoff -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting:
145	
146	```sh
147	riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
148	  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
149	```
150	
151	- Use your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `./andesim doctor` reports).
152	- `-B` points gcc at the runtime artifacts; use the absolute path when
153	  compiling outside the repo.
154	- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's `crt0.o`, links
155	  `andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and pins the library order, so no
156	  semihosting library can leak into the link.
157	- Add `v` to `-march` (e.g. `rv64gcv`) for RVV code.
158	
159	For rv32 targets use the rv32 compiler and the rv32 runtime flavor:
160	
161	```sh
162	riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O2 \
163	  -B <andesim>/build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
164	```
165	
166	Custom build system (no gcc driver)? Link the pieces directly:
167	
168	```sh
169	... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
170	  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
171	  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
172	```
173	
174	What the runtime gives your program, on every engine:
175	
176	| Channel          | Behavior                                                       |
177	|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
178	| stdio (fd 0-2)   | `printf` etc. go to the simulator console (a modeled UART)     |
179	| exit code        | `exit(n)` (n < 256) terminates the simulation; `n` becomes the simulator process exit code |
180	| file io (fd > 2) | `open`/`read`/`write` pass through to host files, resolved against the engine's working directory |
181	
182	A `printf` inside a measured ROI works -- but it adds the real UART cycles
183	to your figure. Keep measured kernels I/O-free when you want clean numbers.
184	
185	### 4.2 Mark your region (ROI markers)
186	
187	For `--trigger marker`, wrap the region you want to measure:
188	
189	```c
190	#include <andesim/ROI.h>   /* shipped with the runtime; rides the -B flag */
191	
192	andesim_ROI_begin();
193	my_kernel(a, b, c);
194	andesim_ROI_end();
195	```
196	
197	The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so a marker
198	binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real silicon.
199	Ship one binary; measure when you want.
200
