# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm
```
```bash
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*` and
`hvm-*` / `hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the same three tests for the HVM, the vector
unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no enable
CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has only ONE address window, so the
demos differ by the PATH the accesses take, not by address:

- `demo/hvm` keeps every data access on the VPU's direct path: the QEMU
  phase fills the whole HVM with vector stores, and the vsim ROI
  vector-reads three windows back (bank0 head, the bank boundary, bank1
  tail). `HVM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff and the RTL's
  VPU-to-HVM path sees it.
- `demo/hvm_slave` does everything with scalar loads/stores: on the RTL
  each access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM
  through its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm/       HVM content transport, vector path (VPU -> HVM)
demo/hvm_slave/ the same HVM SRAM through the bus subordinate port
```
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*` and
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash

make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*` and
`hvm_slave-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:


- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*` and
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
```

# Shared configuration
-include Make.var

# Demos that run on every andesim mode (fast / cycle / hybrid).
SUBDIRS := demo/hello demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma \
           demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma

RUN_TARGETS := $(patsubst demo/%,run-%,$(SUBDIRS))

# RUN_TARGETS are deliberately NOT .PHONY: make never matches pattern
# rules (run-%) against .PHONY targets.
.PHONY: all run clean $(SUBDIRS)

all: $(SUBDIRS)

$(SUBDIRS):
	$(MAKE) -C $@

run: $(RUN_TARGETS)

run-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/$* run

# Forward per-mode targets, e.g. `make hello-fast` -> demo/hello hello-fast.
hello-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello $@

lm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm $@

lm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_slave $@

lm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_dma $@

hvm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_slave $@

	$(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode hybrid --trigger pc \
	    --pc-start hdma_check --pc-end hdma_roi_end \

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*` and
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
```

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-gemm
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*` and `gemm-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout


# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-gemm
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*` and `gemm-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/gemm` moves compute instead of data: the ROI runs an 8x8x8
single-precision GEMM written with the standard RVV intrinsics
(`<riscv_vector.h>`, strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works). The
QEMU phase stages A/B and a scalar reference; the vsim ROI computes
C = A x B on the vector unit and compares. `GEMM_OK` means the
intrinsic kernel ran right after the handoff, with no V setup code
inside the ROI. It is built with `-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need
V in the arch string).

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/gemm/      RVV-intrinsic 8x8x8 GEMM computed inside the ROI
```

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-gemm
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*` and `gemm-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/gemm` moves compute instead of data: the ROI runs an 8x8x8 int32
GEMM written with the standard RVV intrinsics (`<riscv_vector.h>`,
strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works). The QEMU phase stages A/B
and a scalar reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector
unit and compares. `GEMM_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after
the handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
accepts it.

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/gemm/      RVV-intrinsic 8x8x8 GEMM computed inside the ROI
```

# Shared configuration
-include Make.var

# Demos that run on every andesim mode (fast / cycle / hybrid).
SUBDIRS := demo/hello demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma \
           demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma demo/gemm

RUN_TARGETS := $(patsubst demo/%,run-%,$(SUBDIRS))

# RUN_TARGETS are deliberately NOT .PHONY: make never matches pattern
# rules (run-%) against .PHONY targets.
.PHONY: all run clean $(SUBDIRS)

all: $(SUBDIRS)

$(SUBDIRS):
	$(MAKE) -C $@

run: $(RUN_TARGETS)

run-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/$* run

# Forward per-mode targets, e.g. `make hello-fast` -> demo/hello hello-fast.
hello-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello $@

lm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm $@

lm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_slave $@

lm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_dma $@

hvm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_slave $@

hvm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_dma $@

gemm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/gemm $@

clean:
	@for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do $(MAKE) -C $$dir clean; done

-include ../../Make.var

all: gemm.elf gemm.dump

# RVV intrinsics need V in the arch string; the later -march wins.
gemm.elf: main.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -march=rv$(XLEN)gcv $< -o $@

gemm.dump: gemm.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d $< > $@

# The four andesim modes, one target each. Same ELF everywhere.
gemm-fast: gemm.elf
	$(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode fast $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) $<

gemm-cycle: gemm.elf
	$(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode cycle --engine $(ENGINE) $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) $<

gemm-hybrid-marker: gemm.elf

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F4 contract: HTIF file syscalls behave identically on both engines. The
# SAME vplat_file.elf creates/writes/reads/removes a host file (served by
# vsim's sim_control HTIF table and by QEMU's andes_sim_control mirror),
# prints "file io ok" and exits 0. Run in a scratch cwd; the tmp file must
# be gone afterwards (remove() worked host-side).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_file.elf"
SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
QEMU="${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"
[ -x "$QEMU" ] || fail "qemu not found (source ./setup.sh): $QEMU"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_file.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"

run_leg() {  # LABEL CMD...
  local label="$1"; shift
  local wd out rc
  wd=$(mktemp -d)
  out=$( cd "$wd" && timeout 120 "$@" </dev/null 2>&1 ); rc=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'file io ok' \
    || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: missing 'file io ok': $out"; }
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: exit code $rc != 0"; }
  [ ! -e "$wd/vplat_file_test.tmp" ] \
    || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: tmp file not removed"; }
  rm -rf "$wd"
  echo "[ok] $label: file io ok, clean exit, tmp removed"
}

run_leg cycle "$SIM" "$ELF"
run_leg fast "$QEMU" -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios "$ELF"

# rv32 leg (guarded): on rv32 the tohost command reaches the device as TWO
# 32-bit halves (0x10 low, 0x14 high) instead of one 64-bit store, so it
# exercises a distinct device path. Skips when the rv32 toolchain, runtime,
# or qemu-system-riscv32 is absent.
QEMU32="${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv32"
GCC32="$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc"
if [ -x "$QEMU32" ] && [ -x "$GCC32" ] && [ -d "$ROOT/build/runtime/rv32" ]; then
  ELF32=$(mktemp -t vplat_file32.XXXXXX.elf)
  "$GCC32" -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -B "$ROOT/build/runtime/rv32" \
    -specs=andesim.specs "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_file.c" -o "$ELF32" \
    || fail "rv32 fixture build failed"
  run_leg fast-rv32 "$QEMU32" -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-a45 \
    -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios "$ELF32"
  rm -f "$ELF32"
else
  echo "[skip] fast-rv32 leg: rv32 toolchain/runtime/qemu not available"
fi

ok "F4 vplat_file.elf HTIF file io parity (cycle + fast, incl. rv32 halves)"

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-gemm
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*` and `gemm-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/gemm` moves compute instead of data: the ROI runs an 8x8x8 int32
GEMM written with the standard RVV intrinsics (`<riscv_vector.h>`,
strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works). The QEMU phase stages A/B
and a scalar reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector
unit and compares. `GEMM_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after
the handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
accepts it.

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/gemm/      RVV-intrinsic 8x8x8 GEMM computed inside the ROI
```

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-gemm
make run-syscall
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `gemm-*` and `syscall-*` targets work the
same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.

each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works). The QEMU phase stages A/B
and a scalar reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector
unit and compares. `GEMM_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after

`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel

vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
accepts it.

binary: stdout (UART), file io and `gettimeofday()` (HTIF, served

host file descriptors live in the engine process and do not cross the

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)

- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-gemm
make run-syscall
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `gemm-*` and `syscall-*` targets work the
same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/gemm` moves compute instead of data: the ROI runs an 8x8x8 int32
GEMM written with the standard RVV intrinsics (`<riscv_vector.h>`,
strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works). The QEMU phase stages A/B
and a scalar reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector
unit and compares. `GEMM_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after
the handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
accepts it.

`demo/syscall` exercises the runtime's syscall channels with one
binary: stdout (UART), file io and `gettimeofday()` (HTIF, served
host-side -- `fopen`/`fread` hit real files in the working directory),
and the exit code (SimControl). The QEMU phase writes a
time-of-day-seeded payload to a host file and CLOSES it; the vsim ROI
runs a `printf`, reopens and reads the file back, and removes it.
`SYSCALL_OK` means both legs talked to the same host filesystem. It
also shows the two hybrid rules: close files before the handoff (host
file descriptors live in the engine process and do not cross -- closed
files do), and put must-run code inside the ROI (a hybrid run ends at
the exit trigger, so nothing after the ROI executes; the pass signal on
hybrid is the printed `SYSCALL_OK`, while fast and cycle also check
main's return value through SimControl).

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/gemm/      RVV-intrinsic 8x8x8 GEMM computed inside the ROI
demo/syscall/   stdio, host file io and exit code on every mode
```

*.elf
*.dump
*.log
*.tmp

# Shared configuration
-include Make.var

# Demos that run on every andesim mode (fast / cycle / hybrid).
SUBDIRS := demo/hello demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma \
           demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma demo/gemm demo/syscall

RUN_TARGETS := $(patsubst demo/%,run-%,$(SUBDIRS))

# RUN_TARGETS are deliberately NOT .PHONY: make never matches pattern
# rules (run-%) against .PHONY targets.
.PHONY: all run clean $(SUBDIRS)

all: $(SUBDIRS)

$(SUBDIRS):
	$(MAKE) -C $@

run: $(RUN_TARGETS)

run-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/$* run

# Forward per-mode targets, e.g. `make hello-fast` -> demo/hello hello-fast.
hello-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello $@

lm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm $@

lm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_slave $@

lm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_dma $@

hvm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_slave $@

hvm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_dma $@

gemm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/gemm $@

syscall-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/syscall $@

clean:
	@for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do $(MAKE) -C $$dir clean; done

-include ../../Make.var

all: syscall.elf syscall.dump

syscall.elf: main.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $< -o $@

syscall.dump: syscall.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d $< > $@

# The four andesim modes, one target each. Same ELF everywhere.
syscall-fast: syscall.elf
	$(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode fast $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) $<

syscall-cycle: syscall.elf
	$(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode cycle --engine $(ENGINE) $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) $<

syscall-hybrid-marker: syscall.elf
	$(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine $(ENGINE) $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) $<

syscall-hybrid-pc: syscall.elf
	$(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode hybrid --trigger pc \
	    --pc-start syscall_roi --pc-end syscall_roi_end \
	    --engine $(ENGINE) $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) $<

run: syscall-fast syscall-cycle syscall-hybrid-marker syscall-hybrid-pc

clean:
	- rm -f syscall.elf syscall.dump syscall_demo.tmp

.PHONY: all run clean syscall-fast syscall-cycle syscall-hybrid-marker syscall-hybrid-pc

# Path to your andesim checkout, already built with scripts/build_all.sh.

# Cycle-accurate engine for --mode cycle / hybrid.

# Compiler optimization flag
OPT_LEVEL ?= -O2

# Extra flags for every andesim invocation, e.g. --log-level 1
ANDESIM_FLAGS ?=

# ---- Do not touch the followings ----

ANDESIM_BIN := $(ANDESIM)/andesim
RUNTIME := $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime

CC := $(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)gcc
OBJDUMP := $(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)objdump

# One ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid: link against the andesim runtime
# (UART stdio + SimControl exit, no semihosting). -B also puts the runtime's
# include/ on the search path, so <andesim/ROI.h> works.
CFLAGS := -march=rv$(XLEN)gc -mabi=lp64d $(OPT_LEVEL) \
          -B $(RUNTIME) -specs=andesim.specs

# cycle-accurate figure and still validates the CRCs).

                 -DITERATIONS=$(ITERATIONS) -DSEED_METHOD=SEED_VOLATILE \

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-gemm
make run-syscall
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `gemm-*` and `syscall-*` targets work the
same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/gemm` moves compute instead of data: the ROI runs an 8x8x8 int32
GEMM written with the standard RVV intrinsics (`<riscv_vector.h>`,
strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works). The QEMU phase stages A/B
and a scalar reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector
unit and compares. `GEMM_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after
the handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
accepts it.

`demo/syscall` exercises the runtime's syscall channels with one
binary: stdout (UART), file io and `gettimeofday()` (HTIF, served
host-side -- `fopen`/`fread` hit real files in the working directory),
and the exit code (SimControl). The QEMU phase writes a
time-of-day-seeded payload to a host file and CLOSES it; the vsim ROI
runs a `printf`, reopens and reads the file back, and removes it.
`SYSCALL_OK` means both legs talked to the same host filesystem. It
also shows the two hybrid rules: close files before the handoff (host
file descriptors live in the engine process and do not cross -- closed
files do), and put must-run code inside the ROI (a hybrid run ends at
the exit trigger, so nothing after the ROI executes; the pass signal on
hybrid is the printed `SYSCALL_OK`, while fast and cycle also check
main's return value through SimControl).

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/gemm/      RVV-intrinsic 8x8x8 GEMM computed inside the ROI
demo/syscall/   stdio, host file io and exit code on every mode
```
